title: Fleet protection and autoscale observability overhaul to address intermittent capacity shortfalls
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Summary: Intermittent capacity shortfalls in Dedicated pools observed across three regions (us-west1, eu-west1, ap-southeast1) causing increased 429s and latency spikes over the last 10 days. Initial detection came from Canary SLO alerts and customer reports (high-priority accounts observed request failures during peak windows). Investigation shows a scaling regression in the autoscaler: evaluation cadence and thresholding combined with a recent scheduler refactor caused delayed scale-ups under certain traffic burst patterns. KV-cache pressure and degraded packing also amplified the effect, increasing per-request GPU time and exhausting headroom.

Impact: Brief but severe drops in available concurrent tokens for reserved capacity customers, increased error rates for dedicated routes, and missed latency SLOs for several enterprise tenants. Business: manual escalations from two customers; temporary workarounds were applied (throttle/burst reservations).

What happened (high-level):
- A scheduler change (PR #GH-2416) modified lease duration semantics and inadvertently increased autoscaler's perceived load stabilization window.
- Autoscaler evaluation loop uses a 30s rolling window and a heuristic that downweights short bursts; with the new scheduler timings, bursts were blurred and scale-up decisions delayed.
- Node packing heuristics did not account for quantized model variants; the cluster filled with less-efficient placements, increasing per-request GPU usage.
- Monitoring signal drift: the global token consumption metric (tokens/sec) was aggregated incorrectly at the edge aggregation tier, reporting 5-12% lower instantaneous load during bursts.

Immediate mitigations taken:
- Rolled back the scheduler lease change to previous semantics in us-west1 (hotfix GH-PR-2439) to restore expected timing characteristics.
- Deployed emergency autoscale override that increases scale-up aggressiveness for flagged dedicated pools (feature flag rollout: autoscale_rapid_heal=true).
- Applied manual temporary burst capacity reservations for impacted customers to preserve SLAs.
- Re-calibrated alert thresholds and created a transient dashboard to visualize per-pool evaluation latency and token aggregation correctness.

Root cause hypotheses (validated/under investigation):
- Primary: scheduler refactor altered lease/heartbeat timings leading to longer perceived stabilization windows (validated by timeline correlation and repro in staging).
- Secondary: aggregation bug at the edge metrics tier reduced burst visibility (repro in staging; fix targeted).
- Tertiary: packing and quantization mismatch produced higher per-request GPU occupancy during certain model variants (ongoing profiling).

Proposed immediate action items (next 72 hours):
1) Stabilize production: finalize rollback for scheduler semantics across all regions if rollout still active. Owner: Liam O'Connor. Due: 2025-02-21.
2) Autoscaler quick-fix: revert to previous evaluation cadence and lower smoothing window for dedicated pools; add a rapid-heal mode. Owner: Priya Rao. Due: 2025-02-22.
3) Metrics hotpatch: patch edge aggregation to expose instantaneous token rates and add a 'burst_visibility' gauge. Owner: Diego Alvarez. Due: 2025-02-23.
4) Customer remediation: outreach and credits to affected customers plus checklist for manual reservation fallback. Owner: Customer Success / Solutions ENG. Due: 2025-02-24.

Medium-term roadmap (2–6 weeks):
- Observability overhaul: build an autoscale diagnostics pipeline that emits raw evaluation windows, decision deltas, and candidate node placements to a tracing backend.
- Autoscaler improvements: move to an adaptive evaluation window that shortens during high-variance conditions and introduces model-aware packing heuristics.
- Hardening: add chaos tests in staging that simulate bursty traffic with mixed model variants to validate scaling behavior.
- Runbook updates: expand the dedicated-capacity runbook with explicit rollback steps for scheduler changes and an autoscale override playbook.

Long-term (quarter):
- Replace edge aggregation with a streaming, lossless telemetry pipeline for critical SLO signals.
- Evaluate predictive scale-up (learned burst prediction) and incorporate reservation buffer policies for enterprise tenants.
- Continuous profiling to detect quantization/packing inefficiencies and automated suggestions to console Optimize.

Open questions and trade-offs considered:
- Increasing autoscale aggressiveness reduces latency risk but raises cost and transient over-provisioning risk for reserved pools. We propose a controlled feature-flag rollout with per-customer budget caps.
- Rollback vs. forward-fix: rollback is quickest for immediate recovery, but we need to ensure forward-fix addresses metric drift to avoid recurrence.

Acceptance criteria for Done:
- Scaling regression is mitigated (SLO alerts down to baseline for 72 hours).
- New diagnostics pipeline sheds root-cause data for at least two reproduced burst scenarios.
- Runbook and Pager duty playbooks updated and verified in a scheduled chaos test.

Artifacts and references:
- Emergency rollback PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/2439
- Autoscale override PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/autoscaler/pull/1142
- Incident dashboard: https://grafana.redwood-inference.prod/d/abc123/dedicated-autoscale-incident
- Preliminary postmortem doc (internal Confluence): https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/INF/pages/DEDICATED-AUTOSCALE-INCIDENT-2025-02
- Heap/profile traces (staging): gs://redwood-profiles/2025-02/autoscale-burst-profiles.tar.gz

Risks:
- Hotfix rollbacks could expose other subtle timing assumptions; we will gate rollbacks behind canary traffic and monitor additional metrics.
- Over-aggressive autoscale change without budget controls could increase reserved pool spend unexpectedly.

Next steps (today):
- Finalize and merge scheduler rollback across regions (PR verification, ops coordination).
- Gate autoscale override behind telemetry flag and monitor for cost delta.
- Schedule postmortem review with cross-functional attendees (SRE, Serving, Autoscale, Observability, Product) for 2025-02-26.
